driver_side_rules: Do not use `unsafe` in driver code, including `unsafe impl`, `unsafe fn`, or `unsafe {}` blocks.
Do not reference `bindings::*` directly from driver code; keep all PHYLIB interaction inside `kernel::net::phy`.
Do not add raw pointer manipulation or direct MDIO register FFI calls in `drivers/net/phy/et1011c_rust.rs`.
Keep driver logic restricted to the callback set declared in `translation-plan.json`.

obligations.obligation: All `unsafe` inside the existing Rust PHY abstraction must remain confined to that abstraction boundary and continue to rely only on the documented PHYLIB lifetime and locking invariants.
obligations.preferred_discharge: Keep driver code zero-unsafe, extend the PHY abstraction only through safe wrapper methods, and preserve the structural rules for registration, callback trampolines, and typed register access.

obligations.obligation: The Rust PHY registration object must keep the registered driver tables pinned and unregister them exactly once during teardown.
obligations.preferred_discharge: Use the existing `phy::Registration` RAII wrapper and keep raw register/unregister calls inside `rust/kernel/net/phy.rs` only.

obligations.obligation: PHY callback trampolines may create short-lived Rust references from `phy_device *`, but the aliasing and lifetime assumptions must remain localized to the PHY abstraction layer.
obligations.preferred_discharge: Keep all pointer-to-reference conversion inside the callback trampolines in `rust/kernel/net/phy.rs`.

obligations.obligation: All raw PHYLIB/MDIO register FFI must stay behind typed register wrappers so driver code never owns raw pointers or unchecked register access.
obligations.preferred_discharge: Expose reads and writes through `phy::Device` plus typed `reg::Register` implementations only.

obligations.obligation: The generic autoneg helper used by `et1011c` must remain behind a safe `phy::Device` method so driver code never calls PHYLIB FFI directly.
obligations.preferred_discharge: Expose `genphy_config_aneg()` as a safe method on `phy::Device` and keep the unsafe call inside `rust/kernel/net/phy.rs`.
